subject.title: RFC: Standard Hosting Profiles and Ready Check

question: Should OpenClaw own named hosting profiles as stable core support contracts, or standardize only reusable readiness conditions first?
rationale: The RFC creates lasting configuration, API, operational, security-adjacent, and release commitments whose permanent support boundary cannot be chosen from document correctness alone.

options.title: Approve readiness foundation first
options.body: Accept the canonical condition/result model and unchanged default local behavior while deferring non-local profiles to separate decisions.

options.title: Approve the full matrix
options.body: Commit to local, container, reverse-proxy, and node-mode as release-tested core contracts with their strict validation behavior.

options.title: Retain unprofiled readiness
options.body: Improve generally applicable readiness facts while leaving named hosting-posture composition to hosts or external tooling.

recommendation.title: Approve readiness foundation first
recommendation.body: Accept the canonical condition/result model and unchanged default local behavior while deferring non-local profiles to separate decisions.

likelyOwner.reason: Prior review routing and recent repository history make steipete the best available owner for the core support-boundary decision.
